root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence does not establish a single productive primary signification for this root. Its securely Quran-attested lexical item is the temporal noun تَارَةٌ, while تَوْرٌ and the derived forms preserve distinct Classical Arabic branches.
root_idea.development: The history of تَارَةٌ is disputed: it is reported as originally containing و, and a Quran-focused explanation connects its sense of recurrence with the closing or healing of a wound. تَوْرٌ meaning “messenger” is independently attested as a genuine Arabic word. These proposals describe lexical development or association, not a direct meaning of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested form group is displayed under the normalized noun citation form تَارَةٌ.

senses.definition: A time or occasion; once, or again on another occasion.
senses.usage_conditions: A temporal noun that can denote a time of either long or short duration, a single occurrence, or a recurrence. In the Quranic constructions تَارَةً أُخْرَى and تَارَةً بَعْدَ تَارَةٍ, it expresses another time, another turn, or repeated occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to run or flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An obsolete Form I verb; the cited imperfect is يَتُورُ and the verbal noun is تَوْرٌ.
A rare reported form, presented as an apparent variant of ثُئِرَ; no restriction to the illustrative object is implied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return to someone or something repeatedly, time after time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III, used transitively in the cited form and equated with عَاوَدَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repeat an action or do it again, time after time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV, generally transitive in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look sharply or intently at someone or something, or to cast or shoot at it repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV repeated-action construction; the alternatives concern repeated looking and repeated casting or shooting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be encompassed or encircled in order to be captured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the passive construction يُتَارُ عَلَى أَنْ يُؤْخَذَ; another transmitted interpretation takes the expression as repeated shooting, covered separately under أَتَارَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A messenger who goes between people, especially one who carries messages between lovers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical noun with the plural أَتْوَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A girl sent to carry messages between lovers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine lexical form for the specified messenger use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small drinking vessel, also used for water in ablution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A vessel variously described as made of brass or stone; its use for ablution is a conventional specialization.
A compound expression specifying the vessel's material and cooking use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The green substance that spreads over stagnant water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical expression equated with طُحْلُبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blood-revenge or vengeance for a slain person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tentative interpretation in the vocative expression يَا تَارَاتِ فُلَانٍ; one account treats the form as a transposition from وِتْرٌ in the sense of blood-revenge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Applying oneself constantly or perseveringly to work after a period of remissness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of renewed, sustained application.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form IV entry.

cautions: The relationship among the root's lexical branches is not settled by the supplied evidence; in particular, the etymology of تَارَةٌ is reported with competing analyses.
The blood-revenge senses are rare and explicitly reported as variant or tentative interpretations rather than as the ordinary temporal meaning of تَارَةٌ.
